summary: Feature locality can trade one navigation problem for duplication, ambiguous ownership, and harder platform-wide work.

points.text: Cross-cutting capabilities such as authentication, observability, design systems, and persistence rarely belong cleanly to one feature; forcing them into feature folders can duplicate logic or hide shared ownership.

Layer-oriented work remains common. A security review of every data-access adapter or a framework migration across all controllers may be easier when comparable artifacts have an explicit shared boundary and search convention.
Small projects can acquire needless nesting and boilerplate. When a feature has only one or two files, the extra hierarchy may slow navigation without delivering meaningful encapsulation.
Moving code to match changing product terminology creates import churn and history noise; repository-wide tools and stable module APIs may provide more value than strict physical proximity.
